concern.question: Which review gate applies to release branches?

says: A repository checkout, the person alice and the Team platform each keep an Instructions collection naming one source at an exact revision. All three declare a unit for the concern review.approval; the Team's source also declares release.checklist, which no other layer answers. Composing a session start over all three scopes must come back with the order repository, personal, Team: the repository unit wins review.approval, the personal and Team units for it are named shadowed by that winner (not dropped), and the Team's release.checklist unit still wins because nothing higher answers it. When the Team then submits a collection that tries to outrank the repository with a field of its own, admission refuses it (unknown_field): a lower collection's content has no spelling that rewrites the layer order. alice then adds an unkeyed style note to her personal collection and starts a session in her personal scope with no repository: the order is personal then Team, her review unit wins, the Team's is shadowed by it, the unkeyed note is delivered as layered prose in its labelled personal layer, and the Team release unit still wins.  Each of the three also keeps a knowledge collection naming one glossary.terms unit: composing the repository session likewise resolves repository first, then alice's, then the Team's, both losers shadowed rather than dropped. The Team's own collection also carries a second unkeyed note, so the personal-scope session keeps two layers of unkeyed prose, personal then Team, each separately labelled. What must not happen: a whole higher collection hiding the unrelated Team unit, the default order changing silently, or a lower collection reordering the layers.
